title: Retirement Roadmap and Customer Migration Sprints
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: retire legacy model routing and the /v1/legacy-generate endpoint with minimal customer disruption. This ticket coordinates cross-functional launch planning: phased retirements, an explicit migration runway composed of sprints per customer segment, release-note cadence, and all customer-facing templates (emails, in-console banners, changelog entries). We will provide automated compatibility shims for common SDKs, a list of targeted customer migrations (by usage and revenue), and a fallback policy for high-risk customers. Success means >=95% of active usage migrated to supported endpoints before the hard cutoff and clear audit trail for communications and approvals.
acceptance_criteria: Public deprecation notice published and pinned in Console + API docs at least 90 days before hard cutoff
Migration guide (step-by-step) published and validated with two pilot customers representing high, medium usage
SDK adapters (Node/Python/Go) merged and released to package registries with migration examples
Release notes and comms templates reviewed and approved by Legal, Security, and Support
Runbook created for rollback/fallback scenarios and tested in staging canary
Telemetry dashboards show migration progression and error surface; alerts for stalled migrations configured
communication_plan: Phase 0 (internal): Week -8 to -6: product and sales all-hands; share GTM playbook, support runbook, and escalation contacts. Phase 1 (early notice): Week -6: publish deprecation in docs, send segmented email to customers using legacy endpoints, create in-console notice for admin users. Phase 2 (migration assistance): Week -5 to -1: targeted outreach to top 50 customers, offer migration workshops, provide migration PR templates and SDK adapters. Phase 3 (cutover prep): Week -2: final reminder email and banner with hard cutoff date + support hours. Phase 4 (cutover): Day 0: soft block for requests to legacy endpoint with clear error message and migration link; Day 7: enforce hard block. All outbound copy must use approved templates linked below; translations for EU/EMEA customers to be staged by Week -4.
rollout_timeline: 2025-12-15: Internal kick-off and stakeholder sign-off (product, eng, support, legal, security)
2025-12-22: Publish public deprecation notice and release approximation of hard-cutoff date (90-day window)
2026-01-05: Publish migration guide + SDK adapter PRs; begin pilot migrations with two customers
2026-01-12: First migration sprint — top revenue customers engaged, weekly progress dashboard opened
2026-01-26: Second migration sprint — self-serve customers surfaced via in-console helper and CLI tool
2026-02-09: Final reminders and extended support hours for last-mile migrations
2026-02-15: Hard cutoff enforced (requests to legacy endpoint return deprecation error). Post-cutoff monitoring window: 14 days
2026-03-01: Post-cutoff review and retrospective; capture learnings and update playbook
migration_assets: in-console migration helper component designs and copy
qa_checks: End-to-end test: SDK adapter converts legacy call to new API and preserves headers/metadata
Canary: routing fallback to legacy variant in staging and validation of error messages
Docs: verification script ensures all examples reference new endpoint and no 404s remain
Telemetry: dashboard surfaces per-customer migration percentage and migration failure reasons
Support readiness: triage runbook validated by Support on 3 simulated migration incidents
post_mortem_plan: After the 14-day monitoring window, collect telemetry and support logs, hold a cross-functional retro within 1 week, publish a short public summary of impact (customer count, incidents, uptime), and fold action items into the versioning playbook. Particular focus areas: communications effectiveness, top migration blockers, SDK gaps, and billing mapping anomalies. Identify three improvements to implement ahead of the next retirement event.
